text:
Opening keynote at Fintech Builders Summit this morning: Helena Voss-Marchetti, founder and CEO of Larchmont Systems, on why small banks are losing the fraud fight.

Her claim: community banks lose more to fraud per account than large banks because they buy rules, not models. Larchmont's customers are banks under $5B in assets, and most have no data-science team.

Her answer is one shared model across 90 banks, trained on pooled, anonymised fraud labels. A bank without a data-science team gets the benefit of a model built from all 90.

The line of the morning: "A rule you can't update by Friday is a rule the fraudsters already know."

She also expects regulators to require explainable fraud decisions within two years. That's a prediction, but it comes from someone with 20 years in payments infrastructure, a prior payments company founded and sold, and a seat on two bank boards.

My GTM takeaway: when you sell to institutions that can't build it themselves, you're selling an outcome, not a toolkit. And explainability may soon be a requirement rather than a feature.

What are you hearing from community banks on fraud?
